$comment: ★★★ A DENSE SWITCH LAID OUT AFTER A BLOCK-INSERTING PASS (P69, D-LIR-DESCRIPTOR-BLOCK-IDS-SHIFTED-BY-A-BLOCK-INSERTING-PASS). A jump table names its case blocks from DATA, by MIR→LIR's block ids, and the pipeline binds them after assembly to the FINAL module's offsets; a block id is an arena position, so every block a later pass inserts renumbers every block after it. Two passes insert: the inline-asm expansion (a template's label becomes a block) and, under a calling convention that walks the guard page, the calling convention itself (each runtime stack descent gets the walk's loop blocks). Shapes, each its own exit bit: a switch BEFORE both (the control, 1), the template's loop (2), a switch in a function after the template's (4), a template and a switch in one function (8), a VLA frame (16), a switch in a function after the VLA's (64), a VLA and a switch in one function (128). ✔MEASURED 2026-10-07 on the build at 71648598 (the probe shapes of bits 4 and 8): DSS ran them to 2 — the switch dispatched to the wrong cases — on pe and elf, while gcc and clang (c2x and -O2) and mingw gcc ran them to 42 (gnu run 20261007-110129-0d8ce32e, mingw run 20261007-110212-2f16adc9), and the BEFORE control was 42 everywhere. The bits 64 and 128 shapes exist only on a target whose calling convention walks the guard page (pe64); elsewhere they are controls.
